text:
maya: heads-up: after today's merged PR #4321 (commit a1b2c3d) canary we've seen p99 tail latency on INT8/AOT kernels spike.
eng-ci-bot: perf/job bench/latency-e2e-quant FAILED: p99 +45% vs baseline (see job 7843).
liam: saw it too, repro on my laptop with --repack-mode=fast --seed=42.
nora: any flamegraphs or logs?
maya: quick snippet from the perf run:
```
model: redwood-13b-int8
baseline p95: 84ms p99: 210ms
post-merge p95: 88ms p99: 310ms
hot path: dequant_unroll -> kv_cache_lookup -> memcpy
```
samir: p95 barely moves but p99 jumps — smells like rare KV cache thrash or a slow kernel selected for long tails.
jamal: can we bisect the merge? suspect the AOT binding change in the codegen.
liam: starting git bisect. bad=HEAD good=a1b2b3c (marker commit before PR).
eng-ci-bot: git bisect initiated by liam. tracking bench/latency-e2e-quant.
maya: also seeing a short CPU spike on workers in the same samples; flamegraphs point to memcpy in the dequant path.
nora: simple experiment: force kernel_selector to prefer legacy dequant for sequences <64 to see if tail improves.
samir: added a quick patch to force fallback locally; can somebody run a canary?
maya: patch uploaded: https://phab/internal/D9876. queuing canary now.
eng-ci-bot: canary deploy started: canary/quant-aot-fallback.
liam: canary results coming in: initial numbers show p99 back to ~215ms (baseline-like) but throughput down ~3%.
maya: that indicates kernel choice rather than numeric accuracy. dequant overhead on the AOT path is the culprit for rare cases.
nora: plan proposal: revert the AOT binding change from PR #4321, then iterate on kernel-selection heuristics that consider seq len + kv hit-rate.
jamal: creating revert PR and a follow-up to add a p99 regression test to bench/latency-e2e-quant.
liam: filing the follow-up test now, will include a short tail-case harness.
eng-ci-bot: revert PR created: #4329. CI: presubmit checks queued.
maya: holding the rollout until revert lands and canary validated across at least 2 models (13b-int8 and 7b-int8).
samir: sanity check: eval quality delta on our prompt suite is negligible — no accuracy regression from the fallback.
nora: good to confirm; this is a pure performance regression, not quality.
jamal: tagging oncall @jamal for monitoring :eyes:.
eng-ci-bot: revert merged at 2051234588. canary rollback executed.
liam: final canary p99 stabilized at 212ms, throughput back within 1% of baseline. closing the loop.
maya: thanks team — will open a short postmortem with timeline and action items (kernel selector heuristics + new p99 bench). :tada:
